newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Finmin rebukes SPD's Lafontaine on EMU.
newsitem.headline: German Finmin rebukes SPD's Lafontaine on EMU.

text.p: Germany's Finance Ministry on Monday rebuked Social Democrat (SPD) leader Oskar Lafontaine's comment that an economic stability pact was not needed after Europe's monetary union started because inflation was low.
A ministry spokesman said Lafontaine's remarks "missed the point and were not in keeping with promoting a culture of stability".

Lafontaine had said earlier that he opposed taking too narrow an interpretation of the Maastricht criteria for EMU participation, adding that a three percent ratio of new borrowing to economic output was not written in the treaty.

"That is an invention of the Finance Ministry and the Bundesbank," Lafontaine told a news conference. He urged the government to stop stressing the "reference values" as if they carried the weight of law.

Bonn and Frankfurt have fought hard to push through the stability pact, which envisages automatic fines for countries which fail to comply with the Maastricht deficit limits after EMU, which is planned in 1999.

Lafontaine leads a resurgent opposition, and polls show that a possible "red-green" coalition of SPD and Greens ahead of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's conservative coalition. General elections are due by autumn 1998.
